Government contracting is fucked up.

In a conventional private industry setting, you'd hire a firm. You'd work out the first iteration of the website quickly, pay, and then ask them to make improvements. This could be done over drinks, or here in Texas, in the back of a helicopter shooting wild pigs. It's all pretty informal, and the nice lady who handles accounting would handle the back-end details. It might take a year of continuous feedback to get your product where you want it, but you've always got the option of picking up the phone and asking for a tweak or an additional feature. Hell, the development company might give some stuff to you as freebies, just to guarantee future business.

By comparison, the government contracting process is onerous. You have to ask for everything up front. This is especially problematic in web design or software development. Adjustments are almost impossible to make, since any new expenditure of funds requires you to go back through the contracting process. And that process? Like I said, it's fucked. Not only do you have to go through about four different offices to even get your needs in front of the contracting officer, you have to fill out a ton of paperwork that you don't know how to fill out. In the case of IT, that shit may have to go up as far as the NSA for approval or review... multiple times. Then, the contracting officer has to make sure that the firms bidding have the right diversity mix, as priority must be given to the sliding scale of minority-owned businesses, make sure it's under a certain size, ensure all personnel assigned to the project have all the exact correct qualifications, and so on. Because of all the red tape, and because it's so difficult to get a contract cut, and because they can get away with it, the firms bid probably 200% of what it costs in the private sector, if not more. Like I said, it's a fucking nightmare.
